definitions: Moving from a bad or difficult situation to one that is even worse.
Escaping one trouble only to encounter a greater one.
examples: He left his stressful job, only to find himself out of the frying pan and into the fire with an even more demanding role.
They thought moving cities would solve their problems, but it was out of the frying pan and into the fire.
The company's attempt to fix the issue only led them out of the frying pan and into the fire.
lemma: out of the frying pan and into the fire
synonyms: from the frying pan into the fire
source: out of the frying pan and into the fire
